prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1379; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured's vehicle was struck from behind at a traffic signal. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer and reported a shoulder injury at first contact.

Entry 2: The police report lists the claimant as a passenger in the vehicle and places responsibility for the rear impact on the other driver. The officer's notes match the sequence of events the claimant described.

Entry 3: Scene photos and statements from several witnesses have been received, and each describes the collision as the claimant reported it. The other driver's account agrees on the point of impact.

Entry 4: The driver is named on the policy, and coverage was in force when the loss occurred. Nothing in the file suggests any of the damage happened before the policy started.

Entry 5: The claimant gave a recorded statement describing the impact and the onset of shoulder pain, and it matched the first report on every point. The same account has come up in each conversation since.

Entry 6: Medical records show the injury pattern fits the force of the impact and the reported mechanism. Treatment followed a usual course, and visits tapered off as the claimant's condition improved.

Entry 7: A search of prior records found no earlier injury to the same shoulder. The claimant's regular provider has no record of earlier complaints in that area.

Entry 8: The repair appraisal shows major damage consistent with a rear impact. The appraiser has not yet determined whether all of that damage came from this event.

Entry 9: Records from an earlier claim with another carrier show the same major damage to this vehicle from an accident that was never reported to this insurer. The damage is now being presented as new, and the file has been referred for further review.

Entry 10: The claimant was asked about the earlier records and said the prior event was minor and was not reported. The explanation is consistent with the claimant's previous statements.

Entry 11: The file remains open while the appraiser's supplemental report and an independent medical review are obtained. No coverage decision has been made at this time.
